title: Microsoft Purview: sensitivity label inheritance for Teams meeting artifacts (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, configuration routes and artifact protection behaviour are supported. It distinguishes the government-cloud roadmap target from the documented preview and appropriately leaves the setting's default, cloud availability and specific licensing unresolved.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans configurable inheritance of a Teams meeting's sensitivity label by recordings, transcripts and Loop notes, avoiding manual labelling.
claims.quote: Teams meeting artifacts, including recordings, transcripts, and Loop notes, can now be configured to automatically inherit the sensitivity label from the meeting.

claims.claim: The roadmap identifies this as a Microsoft Purview feature.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Apply meeting label to artifacts is a configurable sensitivity label publishing policy setting.
claims.quote: Configure label policy settings that are specific just to calendar items, Teams meetings, and chat: ... Apply meeting label to artifacts

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The setting automatically applies the meeting's sensitivity label to its recordings.
claims.quote: For Teams meetings, automatically apply the meeting's sensitivity label to recordings and their transcripts (.mp4 files)

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The setting also applies the meeting label to the recordings' transcripts, documented with the .mp4 files.
claims.quote: For Teams meetings, automatically apply the meeting's sensitivity label to recordings and their transcripts (.mp4 files)

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The setting also applies the meeting label to meeting notes in .loop files.
claims.quote: and to meeting notes (.loop files) at the time the artifact is saved to SharePoint or OneDrive.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Scope
claims.claim: Inheritance happens when the artifact is saved to SharePoint or OneDrive.
claims.quote: at the time the artifact is saved to SharePoint or OneDrive.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Later changes to the meeting label do not automatically update the inherited artifact label.
claims.quote: If the meeting label changes later, the inherited label doesn't automatically change.

claims.claim: Learn marks Apply meeting label to artifacts as in preview.
claims.quote: Apply meeting label to artifacts ... This setting is in preview

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[1].note
claims.claim: MP4 sensitivity label support must be enabled or MP4 files are not labelled by the artifact setting.
claims.quote: for MP4 files, requires you to enable sensitivity labeling support for MP4. ... If MP4 support isn't enabled, these files aren't labeled when you select this option.

claims.claim: Encryption labels for MP4 files must use Assign permissions now rather than user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels that apply encryption must be configured with the Assign permissions now option, rather than user-defined permissions.

claims.claim: Recordings respect the access permissions and usage rights in the label's encryption settings.
claims.quote: Recordings respect any access permissions and usage rights from label encryption settings

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Labelled, encrypted recordings support playback in the browser.
claims.quote: Recordings respect any access permissions and usage rights from label encryption settings and can be played directly in a web browser

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Recordings and transcripts with a label that applies encryption cannot be downloaded.
claims.quote: However, if a recording and transcript has a label that applies encryption, you can't download them.

claims.claim: Recordings and transcripts can be downloaded if their label does not apply encryption.
claims.quote: You can download them if the label doesn't apply encryption

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: impact
claims.claim: A downloaded recording or transcript whose label does not apply encryption loses its labelling information.
claims.quote: You can download them if the label doesn't apply encryption, but a downloaded file in this case doesn't retain the labeling information.

claims.claim: A suitably permitted owner or administrator can manually relabel the artifacts using the file's Details pane in SharePoint or OneDrive.
claims.quote: You can, if required, manually relabel these files in SharePoint or OneDrive, by using the file's Details pane.

claims.claim: Changing a label that applies encryption requires appropriate permissions.
claims.quote: As with all sensitivity labels, you must have the appropriate permissions to change a sensitivity label that applies encryption, which is always the case for the meeting owner.

claims.claim: An unlabelled meeting has no meeting sensitivity label for this inheritance setting to copy.
claims.quote: For Teams meetings, automatically apply the meeting's sensitivity label to recordings and their transcripts (.mp4 files), and to meeting notes (.loop files)

claims.claim: No approval step is documented for artifact label inheritance.
claims.quote: Searched: "Apply meeting label to artifacts" default enabled approval role GCC license. Opened sensitivity-labels-meetings and create-sensitivity-labels; inheritance is automatic at save, with no approval step described.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the artifact setting's state on arrival, so defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "Apply meeting label to artifacts" "default". Read roadmap 581739, sensitivity-labels-meetings, create-sensitivity-labels and default-label deployment search excerpts; none states this setting's initial value.

claims.claim: Learn does not state the artifact setting's availability in GCC, GCC High or DoD.
claims.quote: Searched: "Apply meeting label to artifacts" "GCC" and "Apply meeting label to artifacts" default enabled approval role GCC license. Read meetings page and GCC/GCC High deployment search excerpts; none states artifact-setting cloud availability.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Purview service description says sensitivity labelling, including automatic or policy-based labelling, requires Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).

claims.claim: The service description lists manual labelling for Teams online meetings under Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 plus Teams Premium.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 + Teams Premium ... Manual Sensitivity Labeling for Teams online meetings | Included

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Some options on the meetings labelling page cannot be configured without a Teams Premium licence in the tenant.
claims.quote: You won't be able to configure all the options referenced on this page if a Teams Premium license isn't found for your tenant.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence statement specific to the artifact inheritance setting is published beyond the documented labelling and Teams Premium requirements.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "artifact" "inheritance" "licensing" sensitivity label; "Apply meeting label to artifacts" "license" "price" meter. Opened meetings page and Purview service description; neither names a licence specifically for this setting.

claims.claim: The meetings labelling page lists no price or meter for this setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Apply meeting label to artifacts" "license" "price" meter. Read sensitivity-labels-meetings in full and the Purview service description's sensitivity-labelling section; no setting-specific price or meter is given.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects the documented labelling entitlement and additional Teams Premium requirements, without asserting a setting-specific entitlement.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG). ... Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 + Teams Premium

claims.claim: A label configured to protect a meeting must include Files & other data assets, Emails and Meetings in its scope.
claims.quote: make sure the following label scopes are selected: ... Files & other data assets ... Emails ... Meetings ... All three options are needed because of their interdependency.

claims.claim: The meeting label must be published to meeting organisers.
claims.quote: Make sure the label is published to meeting organizers and participants.

claims.claim: The meeting label must also be published to meeting participants.
claims.quote: Make sure the label is published to meeting organizers and participants.

claims.claim: Enforcing label meeting options requires a supported Teams client, with minimum versions documented on Learn.
claims.quote: users must use Teams on the web with Edge or Chrome, or one of the following Teams clients: ... Teams client for Windows: 1.5.00.32158+ ... Teams client for macOS: 1.5.00.32154+

claims.claim: Configured label meeting options cannot be enforced for organisers or participants using clients that do not meet the requirements.
claims.quote: If meeting participants or organizers don't use a Teams client that meets these requirements, the configured label meeting options can't be enforced for these users.

claims.claim: The Purview route Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > Publish label leads into the policy configuration containing Apply meeting label to artifacts.
claims.quote: Apply meeting label to artifacts; linked create-sensitivity-labels page: Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies. On the Label policies page, select Publish label to start the Create policy configuration.

claims.claim: No documented PowerShell or API setting for the artifact inheritance option was found.
claims.quote: Searched: "Apply meeting label to artifacts" PowerShell Set-LabelPolicy AdvancedSettings API. Opened Set-LabelPolicy and create-sensitivity-labels; read New-LabelPolicy, Set-Label and client-advanced-settings search excerpts; none documents the artifact option.

claims.claim: An existing label policy can be edited with Edit Policy.
claims.quote: To edit an existing label policy, select it, and then select the Edit Policy button from the flyout pane

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles $true enables MP4 sensitivity labelling support using SharePoint Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: To turn on support for MP4 video files, use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles parameter: ... Set-SPOTenant -EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles $true

claims.claim: No admin UI control is documented for enabling MP4 sensitivity label support.
claims.quote: Searched: "EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles" "portal". Opened sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-onedrive-files; read video-purview and Set-SPOTenant search excerpts. MP4 enablement is documented through PowerShell, not an admin UI.

claims.claim: EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles also controls sensitivity label behaviour for Clipchamp projects.
claims.quote: The same setting also controls sensitivity label behavior for Clipchamp projects.

claims.where: controls[0].scope; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Label policy settings apply to the users and groups selected for publication, allowing a pilot group of organisers.
claims.quote: As part of the label policy, you select users and groups to have sensitivity labels and label policy settings.

claims.claim: The SharePoint MP4 setting has tenant scope, with a connected-geo qualification for Multi-Geo organisations.
claims.quote: The setting applies across the tenant, or the connected geo-location in a Multi-Geo organization

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Multi-Geo tenants must connect to each geo-location and run the MP4 enablement command separately.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo, you must connect to each of your geo-locations and run the command separately.

claims.claim: Administrators should allow 24 hours for label and policy changes to propagate before troubleshooting.
claims.quote: For labels and label policy settings, allow 24 hours for the changes to propagate through the services.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy documents an advanced setting for mandatory meeting labelling.
claims.quote: TeamworkMandatory: Outlook and Teams apps that support this setting can enable or disable mandatory labeling for meetings.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy documents an advanced setting for default meeting labels.
claims.quote: teamworkdefaultlabelid: Outlook and Teams apps that support this setting apply a default label, or no label for meetings.

claims.claim: Learn's description of the artifact setting does not itself name a configuration role.
claims.quote: Searched: "Apply meeting label to artifacts" default enabled approval role GCC license. Read the setting description on sensitivity-labels-meetings; it names no configuration role. This is not a claim that general label-management permissions are undocumented.
